digest.en: Russia strikes a Kyiv bridge as Friedrich Merz arrives with drone interceptors. Brazil’s election pits Lula against Bolsonaro’s son in a test for the pro-Trump Latin American bloc. Bangkok floods turn streets into stagnant lakes while Taiwan buys time with new F-16s.
digest.hi: यूक्रेन में भारतीय फार्मा प्लांट पर रूसी ड्रोन हमले से एक की मौत हुई और 400 करोड़ रुपये का नुकसान हुआ। इसी बीच ईरान ने होर्मुज जलडमरूमध्य खुलवाने के लिए अमेरिका को इस्लामाबाद मेमोरेंडम स्वीकार करने की शर्त रखी है।

articles.title: 3 students arrested over alleged murder of 16-year-old female schoolmate in Johor
articles.summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim ordered a rapid investigation after three students were arrested. They are suspected of murdering 16-year-old Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal. Her body was found covered in blood in a school hall in Yong Peng on Saturday. Malaysia Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has called for a swift probe into the alleged murder of Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal, 16, who died after being found unconscious and covered in blood in a school hall in Yong Peng on Saturday.

articles.title: US Coast Guard searches for missing air ambulance off coast of Massachusetts
articles.summary: The US Coast Guard is searching for a missing air ambulance jet that lost contact with the Federal Aviation Administration early Saturday. The aircraft was conducting a medical evacuation from Bermuda to Boston with six people onboard. The FAA issued a search and rescue alert after the plane failed to check in. Search operations are currently underway off the coast of Massachusetts.

articles.title: Russia Strikes Kyiv Bridge As Merz Arrives With Drone Interceptors
articles.summary: Russia warned foreign diplomats to leave Ukraine or face mortal danger as it vowed to escalate air strikes on Kyiv. President Zelenskyy stated Ukraine will respond to the intensified Kremlin campaign. The threat targets non-citizens currently in the country. Russia has vowed to intensify its relentless strikes against Kyiv and warned foreign diplomats and other visitors to leave the country or be exposed to “mortal danger,” while Ukraine's leader said his country will respond to the Kremlin's deadly air campaign.

articles.title: Women declare #IamJaneDoe in solidarity with Cornell University rape victim
articles.summary: Women are using the hashtag IamJaneDoe to support a Cornell University rape victim. The student is distressed by online attempts to reveal her identity. New York law protects her anonymity in sexual assault lawsuits, but skeptics are actively trying to expose her name. And although ‌New York law allows “Jane Doe” anonymity for sexual assault lawsuits, the Cornell student has become distressed at attempts by some ​online skeptics of her account to discover her name and publish it.

articles.title: Popular Mobilisation Forces
articles.summary: Iran-backed Shia groups in Iraq called the September 30 withdrawal of American troops a historic victory. These organizations previously clashed with U. S. forces during the occupation. The timing coincides with ongoing military conflict between Washington and Iran. For the Iran-backed Shia armed organisations, which opposed the U. occupation of Iraq and frequently clashed with U. forces, the September 30 withdrawal of American troops, at a time when Washington wages war on Iran, is a ‘historic victory’.

articles.title: US Lawmakers Target Serbia's Democratic Backsliding, Ties To Russia, China, Iran
articles.summary: A bipartisan group of US lawmakers is demanding stricter measures against Serbia. They cite democratic backsliding, corruption, and expanding Russian, Chinese, and Iranian influence. The pressure arrives just weeks before snap parliamentary elections. A bipartisan, bicameral group of US lawmakers is pressing for tougher action on what they describe as democratic backsliding, corruption, and growing Russian, Chinese, and Iranian influence in Serbia, just weeks before snap parliamentary elections.

articles.title: Ruined And Flooded, Russian-Occupied Oleshky In Ukraine Starves Under A 'Total Blockade'
articles.summary: Residents of Russian-occupied Oleshky in Ukraine's Kherson region face starvation. Land mines and supply cutoffs have created a total blockade. Ukrainian officials describe the area as a starving ghost town. People in Russian-held Oleshky in Ukraine's Kherson region have endured war, occupation, and devastating flooding. Now, trapped by land mines and cut off from basic supplies, they face "hell," starving in a virtual ghost town, Ukrainian officials and volunteers say.

articles.title: Brazil’s neck-and-neck election offers test for growing pro-Trump Latin American bloc
articles.summary: Brazil holds a tight election pitting Lula against the son of a convicted former president. The race tests the growing pro-Trump bloc in Latin America. Trump recently gathered right-wing leaders to promote his regional agenda. The outcome will shape the continent's political alignment. articles.title: Flydubai attack feeds Netanyahu’s ‘protector’ line as polls near
articles.summary: A Flydubai flight carrying 170 passengers faced an attempted hijacking. The pilot and passengers prevented a major disaster. Netanyahu released a video warning of threats shortly before the incident. The event reinforces his narrative of constant security risks for Israel. The apparent attempted hijacking of a Flydubai flight carrying 170 mostly Israeli passengers was another reminder to Israelis of the constant threat of terror and war.

articles.title: New F-16s buy Taiwan time and space against China’s air coercion
articles.summary: Taiwan received its first two F-16V Block 70 jets at Chihhang Air Base. The aircraft provide breathing room against Chinese gray-zone coercion. However, increasing Chinese stealth capabilities limit their wartime utility. The delivery marks a significant step in Taiwan's air defense strategy. Taiwan’s new American-made F-16V Block 70 jets deliver much-needed breathing room against daily Chinese gray-zone coercion, yet surging Chinese stealth numbers and cratered runway risks mean their wartime utility would be sharply contested.

articles.title: Bangkok at breaking point as floods turn streets into stagnant lakes
articles.summary: Bangkok declared a disaster across all 50 districts after severe flooding. Forty people died as streets turned into stagnant lakes. Experts warn extreme flooding will worsen across south-east Asia. The city struggles to absorb sudden downpours during the rainy season. With 40 dead and a disaster declared across all 50 city districts, experts warn extreme flooding will only worsen across south-east AsiaBangkok is used to absorbing the sudden afternoon downpours that inundate the city during the rainy season.

articles.title: Brazil’s Lula says only he can stop rise of fascism under Bolsonaro’s son
articles.summary: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva led a massive rally in Rio de Janeiro on Saturday. He declared himself the sole barrier against the return of far-right "fascists" to power. The event preceded Sunday’s presidential election, which observers view as the most consequential in decades. Lula, eighty years old, framed the vote as a decisive choice between his left-wing government and the political movement associated with former president Jair Bolsonaro.

articles.title: Flydubai Passenger Recounts Saving Stabbed Pilot
articles.summary: A Georgian-Israeli dentist on a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Israel helped a pilot allegedly stabbed by his co-pilot on September 30. Shota Musayev left his wife to assist the injured crew member. He feared for his own survival during the incident. The flight was diverted to safety. Georgian-Israeli dentist Shota Musayev told RFE/RL that he feared he might not survive when he left his wife’s side to help after the lead pilot was allegedly stabbed by his co-pilot during a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Israel on September 30.

articles.title: WHO appeals for massive aid influx ahead of winter
articles.summary: The World Health Organization warned that delayed medical supplies to Gaza risk devastating consequences. Lifesaving medicines and prosthetics are stuck in transit from Israel. The UN agency appealed for a massive aid influx before winter arrives. Palestinians in the enclave urgently need these critical resources. Repeated delays in bringing lifesaving medicines, prosthetics and more from Israel into Gaza risk having devastating consequences on Palestinians who urgently need them in the war-torn enclave, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) said on Friday.

articles.title: Row erupts over Cairo mural depicting Tutankhamun and Nefertiti with dark skin
articles.summary: Cairo authorities removed a 66-metre mural from Tahrir Square before Xi Jinping’s state visit. The artwork depicted Tutankhamun and Nefertiti with dark skin. Critics alleged it revived Afrocentric claims about Pharaohs’ origins. The removal sparked a public row over historical representation. Artwork created in Tahrir Square for Chinese president’s state visit to Egypt is painted over amid allegations it revived Afrocentric claims about Pharaohs’ originsOn the eve of Chinese president Xi Jinping’s state visit to Cairo last month, the city authorities were busy removing a 66-metre-long mural from the esteemed guest’s line of sight. Depicting the Pharaoh Tutankhamun and Queen Nefertiti, t.

articles.title: After Russia's Elections, An Expert On Fraud Is Arrested And Reportedly Beaten
articles.summary: Russian security forces detained fraud analyst Aleksandr Kynev in Moscow after he warned of vote falsifications benefiting United Russia. He was reportedly beaten while in custody. The incident highlights a clash between security agencies and political operatives within the Kremlin. In the days between the elections and his arrest, Aleksandr Kynev had pointed to evidence of falsifications benefitting the United Russia party.

articles.title: US blast simulation targets China’s alleged secret nuke testing
articles.summary: The US Department of Energy conducted underground blast experiments in Nevada. These tests aim to detect clandestine nuclear detonations. The program addresses concerns about China's secret testing capabilities. Faced with rising great-power suspicions and the challenge of verifying clandestine, cavity-muffled detonations, the US is turning to high-precision subterranean blast experiments in the Nevada desert to strip covert nuclear testing of its technical cover.

articles.title: Computer science has long understood how to keep AI under control
articles.summary: A New York Times article claimed OpenAI agents independently launched a cyberattack. Computer scientists reject this framing. They note that AI systems do not act autonomously. Humans design, deploy, and control these tools. The narrative misattributes human agency to software. AI agents don’t go rogue. That’s something only humans do. Nevertheless, a New York Times article – representative of much news coverage of AI – described an OpenAI hacking as “A. I.

articles.title: Kyrgyz Activist Gets 2 Years For Criticizing Growing Chinese Presence
articles.summary: The Lenin District Court in Bishkek found activist and politician Mavlyan Askarbekov guilty and sentenced to two years in prison on offenses related to a law on incitement of racial, ethnic, national, religious, or interregional hatred, a verdict he called "absurd." Kyrgyz Activist Gets 2 Years For Criticizing Growing Chinese Presence.

articles.title: Oil Exports Find A Way Past Iranian Attacks, But Refinery Bottleneck Persists
articles.summary: Exports of crude oil from the Middle East hit their highest level in September since the war with Iran began, reinforcing a trend of increased supplies despite Iranian attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, according to analysis of shipping and commodity market data by industry observers. Oil Exports Find A Way Past Iranian Attacks, But Refinery Bottleneck Persists.

articles.title: Afghanistan’s TTP sanctuary is becoming harder to deny
articles.summary: For years, Pakistan’s claim that the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan operates from sanctuaries inside Afghanistan produced a familiar exchange: Islamabad accused, Kabul denied, and each new militant attack triggered another round of recrimination. That pattern is becoming harder to sustain. The sanctuary dispute can now be tested against a growing body of evidence rather than competing claims [] The p Afghanistan’s TTP sanctuary is becoming harder to deny.

articles.title: Ebola response faces setback as transit centre burns down in DR Congo camp
articles.summary: The enormous challenge of halting the spread of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) just became even harder after a key transit centre for patients requiring treatment burned down in Ituri province. Ebola response faces setback as transit centre burns down in DR Congo camp.

articles.title: Nepal floods threaten jobs and livelihoods beyond disaster zone: ILO
articles.summary: The deadly flash floods in northern Nepal have severely disrupted employment and livelihoods, with wider impacts beyond communities that were directly affected, the International Labour Organization (ILO) said in a preliminary assessment released on Thursday. Nepal floods threaten jobs and livelihoods beyond disaster zone: ILO.

articles.title: Daredevil Jaan Roose completes slackline walk high above central Seoul
articles.summary: Estonian slackliner Jaan Roose completed a 160-metre walk 120 metres above central Seoul on Thursday. The narrow ribbon stretched between the Koreana hotel and the Dong-A Media Center near Gyeongbokgung palace. He succeeded on his second attempt after an initial failure. Lunchtime crowds gathered below to watch the high-altitude feat. High above, a narrow ribbon ran between the Koreana hotel and the Dong-A Media Center, a few hundred metre.

articles.title: Trump administration diverts human rights funds to push far-right agenda abroad
articles.summary: The Trump administration redirected over $175 million from the state department human rights fund. This includes a $40 million grant for an anti-communism fund. Additional support goes to groups advocating for white Afrikaners. The move redefines human rights priorities to align with far-right agendas abroad. Support such as for white Afrikaners and anti-communism reveals how US is redefining what qualifies as human rightsWith hours left before the funding expires, the Trump administration is pushing to direct more than $175m of the state department’s flagship human rights fund to a slate of awards that includes a huge $40m grant for an anti-communism fund, support for a group advancing white Afrikaner.

articles.summary: पुर्तगाल में अमेरिकी सेना के लजेस एयरबेस उपयोग पर विवाद छिड़ा है। वामपंथी दलों ने सरकार पर बिना जांच अनुमति देने का आरोप लगाया। ईरान युद्ध में अमेरिका की मदद का सवाल उठा है। राजनीतिक बवाल बढ़ रहा है। Portugal US military agreement: पुर्तगाल में अमेरिका की ईरान युद्ध में मदद पर बड़ा विवाद छिड़ गया है। वामपंथी दलों ने सरकार पर आरोप लगाया है कि उसने बिना सही जांच के अमेरिकी सेना को लजेस एयरबेस इस्तेमाल करने की अनुमति दे दी।
